children: Corteva posted lower sales and updated its full-year guidance after experiencing challenges from the crop protection market in Brazil.
The company swung to a pro forma loss of $56 million, or 8 cents a share, compared with a profit of $58 million, or 9 cents a share, the year earlier.
On an adjusted pro forma basis, earnings per share were 6 cents.
The agriculture company's third-quarter sales fell 9% to $1.59 billion, below Wall Street expectations of $1.77 billion.

Corteva's Latin America unit experienced pricing pressure after facing competition on molecules late in their lifecycle, the company said. Brazil crop protection markets have become weaker from farmer liquidity constraints, elevated financing costs, just-in-time purchasing and increased pricing pressure, Corteva said.
On a pro forma basis, the agriculture company now expects adjusted operating earnings per share between 76 cents and 80 cents. Analysts polled by FactSet expected 60 cents a share.
Corteva's shares decline 6.6% to $11.34 following the results in post-market trading Wednesday.

The pro forma guidance reflects the company's expectations after the spinoff of its seed business, Vylor, into an independent company. Corteva has exclusively focused on crop protection after the spinoff completed on Oct. 1.
Volume was flat, with growth in all regions except Latin America, Corteva said. The company's North America unit faced pricing headwinds for acetochlor, a herbicide.
Corteva and its subsidiary EIDP on Tuesday said their quarterly filing would be delayed after needing more time to complete processes related to the spinoff.
